summary: USER (2026-06-15, MAIN concern): the GB10 is UNIFIED MEMORY (Grace ARM CPU + Blackwell GPU share 273 GB/s), so ANY non-vLLM compute co-located on the GB10 (the codex agent Docker, the inference_proxy) competes with vLLMs HBM-bound weight read = CONTAMINATES the timing-sensitive speed measurement (s/fwd, run-ahead/OPT-1, accept timing). REBUILD the deployment harness to OFFLOAD everything except vLLM to the x86 box (alienware, reachable over SSH): codex agent + proxy run on alienware, vLLM runs ALONE on the GB10. Confirmed feasible: alienware = x86_64, has docker + the codex-runner:v1 image + swe_eval_offload venv (the SWE eval is ALREADY offloaded there). Architecture: vLLM serve on GB10 (port 9950, reachable from alienware - likely tailscale) <- proxy on alienware (forwards codex->GB10 + pair-dumps) <- codex-runner:v1 Docker on alienware. The deploy-* measurement reads the GB10 vLLM /metrics (clean - the model decode, no contention) + the alienware pair-dumps (synced back) for the lossless rescore (the recurrent oracle is a SEPARATE GB10 GPU phase, also clean). GOAL: during a codex run, the GB10 runs ONLY vLLM (verify via ps/docker on the GB10 = nothing but the vllm container). Build the offloaded harness (update fr13_bigdenom_swe_serve.sh + run_swe_bench_q36_a.py to launch proxy+codex on alienware over SSH; vLLM stays GB10) + validate clean + flag any alienware setup gaps. On fr13-speedfix. Phase1 build (CPU+SSH) -> Phase2 validate (GPU+SSH) -> Phase3 verify. Output FR13_OFFLOAD_HARNESS.md.

b.networkRobustness: (1) s/fwd STAYS network-immune by construction: the deploy-speed brackets are `curl http://127.0.0.1:9950/metrics` read GB10-LOCALLY (bigdenom L383/395, variant L347/359) — never across the wire; request_decode_time_seconds only advances while decoding so a codex stall just pauses it. My changes do not touch this. (2) codex<->vLLM path survives drops: inference_proxy.py upstream POST now reconnects with exponential backoff (LUMO_PROXY_UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_S=1200, _MAX_RETRIES=6, _BACKOFF_S=3) instead of an instant 502 — one blip no longer kills the 30-min task; link-dead after retries returns a distinct 504 'NETWORK-DROP; discard this measurement window'. (3) rsync resilient: _RSYNC_RESILIENT = rsync -az --partial --append-verify --timeout=120 wrapped in the eval-offload _net_retry (5 attempts, backoff) for both the workspace up/down and the pair-dump fetch-back. (4) drop detection + non-mis-attribution: every proxy reconnect logs '[proxy][NET-DROP]...CLASSIFIED network-drop (not a model/measurement failure)'; an SSH transport rc=255 on the remote codex run is classified network_drop (logged to swe_codex_offload_network.log), NOT a degenerate #12 fork; a background link watchdog curls GB10 /health from alienware every 10s logging up/down to offload_link_state.log. (5) wire-stalled window DISCARD + watchdog: if the link is down past OFFLOAD_LINK_DOWN_MAX_S (300s) the watchdog fails LOUD, writes offload_link_dead.flag, the harness writes DEPLOY_SPEED_DISCARDED.flag and sets a distinct rc=12 so a wire-stalled window is flagged-not-recorded; clean remote-proxy teardown on EXIT. (6) measurement side always GB10-local. NOTE: a live blip-injection exercise of these paths is the ValidateClean GPU phase (not run here — CPU/SSH only, no GPU boot).

Functional behavior is correct (task survived); only the reconnect AUDIT TRAIL is missing on the offload path. Suggest piping the offload proxy stderr to a file (e.g. via the --log-path mechanism or a redirect that survives setsid) in a follow-up — would make a real reconnect provable rather than inferred from request wallclock. (3) The B=1 contamination is modest (~8% per-token); the B=4 variant run is the decisive contamination quantification and is the natural next step. (4) Both runs torn down cleanly: GB10 has no containers, alienware has no leftover iptables rule / orphan proxy / orphan codex docker. (5) The eval verdict was "failed" on both arms — EXPECTED, these are bounded AGENT_WALL_S validation runs, not full SWE solves; the health "early-exit" flag on the clean arm is also expected (codex finished in 176s).
